::: {#exm-cube-bipartite}
#### The cube graph is bipartite

Let $Q_3$ be the graph whose vertices are the eight bit strings of length 3,
with an edge between two strings when they differ in exactly one position [@wikipedia_hypercube_graph].
For example, $000$ and $010$ are adjacent (@def-adjacent), but $000$ and $011$ are not.
@fig-cube draws $Q_3$ as the corners and edges of a cube.

Let $V_1$ be the strings with an even number of ones, and $V_2$ the strings with an odd number of ones:

$$
V_1 = \set{000, 011, 101, 110}, \qquad V_2 = \set{001, 010, 100, 111}.
$$

Changing one position of a string changes its number of ones by exactly one,
from even to odd or from odd to even.
So every edge has one endpoint in $V_1$ and the other in $V_2$, and $Q_3$ is bipartite (@def-bipartite).

::: {#fig-cube}
